title: Bryan Johnson's sleep protocol: resting heart rate before bed and 10 tips for high-quality sleep
summary: Bryan treats sleep as a craft to master, anchored on one metric: resting heart rate just before bed. He lays out ten practical rules (early light meal, wind-down, light, consistency, stimulants, temperature, noise, wearable) and says anything that raises pre-bed heart rate degrades sleep.

principles.text: Treat sleep as a craft: be on time to bed like for a meeting, and see yourself as a professional sleeper.
principles.quote: You need to think about sleep as you would anything you take seriously. A a hobby, your job, you know, being a parent, you need to try to perfect the craft.

principles.text: Use resting heart rate before bed as the master metric: what raises it hurts sleep, what lowers it helps.
principles.quote: My sleep depends upon my resting heart rate before bed. And so I've tried to structure my entire life around this idea of things that increase my resting heart rate are bad.

principles.text: Finish eating at least 4 hours before bed; Bryan eats about 8 hours before, and lighter foods help.
principles.quote: you want to have your final meal of the day at least 4 hours before bed. You can experiment with 2, three, four, five, six, seven. I have my last meal of the day around 8 hours or so before my bedtime

principles.text: Do a 30 to 60 minute screen-free wind-down: walk, meditate, breath work, a book in hand.
principles.quote: you need to have a 30 to 60 minute wind down routine every day. Your you can't just finish work and then 30 seconds later you just put your head on the pillow and fall asleep.

principles.text: Get bright light within minutes of waking (Bryan uses a 10,000 lux light at 4:30 a.m.) and keep a consistent bedtime.
principles.quote: I wake up before the sun rises around 4:30 a.m. So, I use a 10,000 lux light in my home.

principles.text: Mind stimulants and blue light: caffeine has a roughly 6-hour half-life, evenings should be red or amber light.
principles.quote: caffeine has roughly a 6 hour half-life. So a cup of coffee at 4 p.m. is a half a cup of coffee in you at 10 p.m. when you're asleep.
